expected_behavior: The requested instrument selects its own holding and the same identity reaches measurement and output
actual_behavior: A shared synthesis route read Kitt Peak flux unconditionally while the instrument argument only labelled the product
root_cause: Instrument-specific flux loader was called inside shared route instead of the holding dispatch
affected_artifacts: Exact historical product paths UNKNOWN; RYA-911/913 record the HARPS-labelled Kitt Peak result
science_impact: The run completed with scientifically invalid cross-instrument provenance
notes_provenance: Historical seed from RYA-911/913 and committed test narrative; run_id/base_sha/exact artifact paths were not recoverable and are intentionally blank/UNKNOWN

product_identity: 1984 NSO Atlas No. 1 segment lm0840 (8400-8441 A)
symptom: lm0840 is 714 bytes of saved HTML, not spectral data; the bundled README is a second saved HTTP 500 page
expected_behavior: A staged atlas segment contains three numeric columns of monotonic air wavelength, pseudo-residual flux and irradiance
actual_behavior: Both staged copies on Sirius held an archived HTTP 500 error page from nispdata.nso.edu in place of 8400-8441 A
root_cause: A failed download was written to disk and propagated to both staged copies; nothing verified the payload was data
affected_files: /mnt/codex-data/spectra/_mac_import_20260816/Solar Calibration/Kitt Peak Flux Atlas/lm0840; /mnt/codex-data/spectra/Solar Calibration/Kitt Peak Flux Atlas/lm0840
affected_artifacts: NONE - no committed Kitt Peak product covers 8400-8440 A; AlI_6910_9199 has no candidate line there
science_impact: No published result corrupted. Latent: the solar line list holds 33 Fe (30 Fe I + 3 Fe II), 61 Co I and 55 CN I candidates in 8400-8440 A that the planned Fe/Fe II Kitt Peak runs would have silently lost
notes_provenance: Re-fetched from https://nispdata.nso.edu/ftp/pub/atlas/fluxatl/lm0840 (154546 bytes, 4067 rows, 8400.004-8440.999 A, sha256 7823350289012fa45a1411a4b30c7c0e2c4edec7d856dc8724a7546cb9ae29b6); corrupt originals quarantined at /mnt/codex-data/codex/kpcross/quarantine

symptom: A corrupt segment was reported as missing wavelength coverage: 'no Kitt Peak segment covers 8420.000 A'
expected_behavior: A segment that exists but cannot be parsed fails loudly and names the file and the reason
actual_behavior: kp_segments() swallowed the parse failure in a bare 'except Exception: continue', dropping lm0840 from the inventory (251 files on disk, 250 inventoried) so load_kp_window raised a coverage-shaped LookupError
root_cause: Bare except around np.loadtxt in the inventory loop conflated 'unreadable' with 'absent'
detected_by: RYA-938, following a data-integrity finding handed over from the RYA-931 telluric work
affected_artifacts: NONE committed; the defect made an absence indistinguishable from a defect (RYA-833)
science_impact: Any line in a corrupt segment's range would be reported as uncovered rather than as a data fault, in any current or future Kitt Peak run
notes_provenance: kp_segments() now validates via pipeline.kp_atlas_integrity and raises KpAtlasCorrupt; allow_corrupt=True is an explicit, recorded opt-in

symptom: Kurucz 2005 showed near-zero line depth where the 1984 atlas and the telluric-free IAG atlas agree on deep lines (Al I 6696: 0.008 vs 0.254/0.257; K I 7699: 0.039 vs 0.808/0.807)
expected_behavior: Line depths compared at a common wavelength medium
actual_behavior: irradthu.dat was read as air (scale=10.0, no conversion), displacing every Kurucz line by the air-vacuum offset (~1.7 A at 6600 A, about 200 sampled pixels), so the tight line window sampled continuum instead of the line
root_cause: The Kurucz header states only 'nm' and never states the medium; RYA-929 read it as air without measuring, and flagged the resulting mismatch as a Kurucz product defect
detected_by: RYA-938 cross-correlation registration test against the 1984 air grid
science_impact: No abundance affected - RYA-929 was explicitly diagnostic and blocked Kurucz line substitution. The window-level GO survives: a 1.7 A shift barely moves a 17-300 A window statistic, which is why the defect showed only at line scale
notes_provenance: Measured lag +1.700 A vs predicted air-vacuum offset +1.697 A (3 mA); IAG positive control returns -0.000 A; after vac_to_air all three windows return -0.000 A and Al I 6696 recovers to 0.248 vs IAG 0.257

symptom: The telluric correction leg could only run on the Mac.
expected_behavior: Compute runs on Sirius (RYA-567); the engine path is resolved, not assumed.
actual_behavior: scripts/rya931_molecfit_model.py hard-coded ESOREX=/opt/homebrew/bin/esorex, so on Sirius it failed before molecfit was even reached.
root_cause: An absolute Mac path literal baked into the runner; molecfit was additionally never installed on Sirius.
affected_artifacts: none - no product was ever produced on Sirius
science_impact: None on committed results. The correction was Mac-only, which is the opposite of the project's Sirius-only-computation rule.
notes_provenance: molecfit 4.4.4-5 built on Sirius from ESO's source kit (cksum 488272865 matches ESO); esorex 3.13.10 and telluriccorr 4.3.3 identical to the Mac; MIPAS equ.fits byte-identical (md5 cf98a77b2e849ba956aba78f7fe1f592).

symptom: A successful molecfit run reported as a failure, with the self-contradicting message 'molecfit_model failed (rc=0)'.
expected_behavior: Product names are a property of the recipe invocation and identical on every machine.
actual_behavior: esorex took --suppress-prefix from ~/.esorex/esorex.rc. The Mac has no rc at all; a fresh ESO source-kit install writes suppress-prefix=FALSE. Under FALSE all ten products are still written, as out_0000..out_0009.fits, so BEST_FIT_MODEL.fits was simply absent.
root_cause: The runner relied on machine-local esorex configuration instead of passing --suppress-prefix=TRUE explicitly.
science_impact: None. A silent-wrong CLASS though: the failure looked like a fit problem and sent the session hunting one that did not exist. The error message now distinguishes a failed recipe from a missing expected product and lists what was produced.
notes_provenance: Found only because a SECOND machine was tried; a single-machine project never sees this class.

symptom: The RYA-929 sweep script still read the Kurucz 2005 product as air after RYA-938 established it is vacuum.
expected_behavior: Kurucz 2005 is converted vacuum->air on read, like every other vacuum product in the repo.
actual_behavior: read_ascii_windows(..., scale=10.0) with no conversion, displacing every line ~1.7 A at 6600 A (~200 sampled pixels).
root_cause: RYA-938 characterised the defect and fixed its own reader, but left the RYA-929 script untouched because that ticket was Done.
detected_by: RYA-939, checking the latent defect RYA-938 flagged out of scope
science_impact: No committed abundance affected. But RYA-933/934 (Kurucz 2005 Fe I / Fe II all-engine reruns) were queued against this script and would have inherited the defect - a line-level table that looks plausible and is displaced by ~200 pixels.
notes_provenance: Fixed by adding an explicit vacuum=True flag to the reader rather than a silent conversion, so the medium is declared at every call site.
